hinge.title: Do the diagonals of a parallelogram have to be equal, bisect each other, or both?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Diagonal is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Do the diagonals of a parallelogram have to be equal, bisect each' is answered as diagonal rather than parallelogram.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: parallelogram still holds here even though Bisection means the intersection point is the midpoint of each diagonal is missing from the stem — on the item about Do the diagonals of a parallelogram have to be equal.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The answer is parallelogram because of the most obvious label, colour, size or printed number in the stem, without using 'Do the diagonals of a parallelogram have to be equal, bisect each' as the operative test.

intelligence.enrichment: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, but they need not be equal.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Mathematics question. Chapter: math/grade_08/ch_104. The student must decide: Do the diagonals of a parallelogram have to be equal, bisect each other, or both? Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Supply exactly one complete tikzpicture. The stem must refer to that figure. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
